title: Attachment Points and Underlying Policy Terms — Excess Flood Tier Table
content:
An Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines) layer pays only above its attachment points, and the attachment points depend on the kind of underlying primary flood policy beneath it. The table states, tier by tier, the attachment points, the kinds of underlying policy accepted and the underlying terms of the tier. Amounts are in US dollars.

| Tier | Excess Flood 250K | Excess Flood 500K | Excess Flood 1M | Excess Flood 2M | Excess Flood 3M | Excess Flood 5M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dwelling attachment point over an NFIP Dwelling Form policy | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 |
| Personal property attachment point over an NFIP Dwelling Form policy | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 |
| Lowest dwelling attachment point accepted over a private primary flood policy | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 | 250000 |
| Lowest personal property attachment point accepted over a private primary flood policy | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 | 100000 |
| Kinds of underlying primary flood policy accepted | NFIP Dwelling Form; private primary | NFIP Dwelling Form; private primary | NFIP Dwelling Form; private primary | NFIP Dwelling Form; private primary | NFIP Dwelling Form; private primary | NFIP Dwelling Form; private primary |
| Excess policy pays inside the attachment point when the underlying lapses or carries less (drop-down) | no | no | no | no | no | no |
| Current declarations of the underlying policy must be on file before binding and at each renewal | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

## Points of judgement

- The two NFIP rows are fixed attachment points: over an NFIP Dwelling Form policy every tier attaches at 250000 for the dwelling and 100000 for personal property.
- The two private-primary rows are floors, not fixed points: over a private primary flood policy the attachment is set at binding from the underlying limits, never below these figures.
- With drop-down set to "no" on every tier, the excess layer never pays inside its attachment point because of a gap in the underlying cover.
